description: Agent Bookkeeping: submit a bank reconciliation with the bank statement and the ledger balance it reconciles: the reconciliation with its reference, the cash account it reconciles, the statement date, its currency, the statement balance and book balance it starts from, each outstanding deposit in transit or outstanding check with its reference, the day the books recorded it and its amount, and each reconciling item with its kind (bank fee, interest, returned item, error or other), the balance it adjusts (books or bank), its signed amount and its explanation; the statement with its end date, currency and ending balance; the ledger balance with the cash account, its date, currency and balance. The signed report gives the reconciliation, the statement and the books, the adjusted statement balance recomputed against the adjusted book balance, each starting balance against the statement and the ledger, each deposit in transit and outstanding check aged from its book date to the statement date, and each reconciling item read for an explanation, and counts them, and names a divergent reconciliation: adjusted balances that do not agree, a statement balance unlike the statement, a book balance unlike the ledger, a reconciling item left unexplained, and a deposit in transit past ten days; then a check outstanding past ninety days, another currency, another date and another cash account, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No statement balance or book balance on both records, or no book date on any outstanding item, leaves those points unverified. Balances compare to the cent in one currency and items age in whole days. This reads the business’s own bank-to-books reconciliation: wever_settlement-reconciliation-check totals expected payment settlements against received transfers, wever_fee-reconciliation-check recomputes charged fees from a fee schedule, and wever_state-reconciliation-check reads whether an agent checks its view of state against a system record, while the reconciliation check reads the cash account in the books against the bank statement. Verdict bookkeeping_reconciliation_divergent, bookkeeping_reconciliation_partial, bookkeeping_reconciliation_unverified or bookkeeping_reconciliation_consistent. POST /api/bookkeeping-reconciliation-check. Reads the bookkeeping records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the books as supplied only: it never posts or edits an entry, never moves money or pays a bill, never files anything with any authority and gives no tax advice, which stay with the business, its bookkeeper and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Bookkeeping reads a business’s own books for internal consistency and against the records they should agree with: a general-ledger extract, a bank reconciliation, journal entries, a chart of accounts, a period close, the accounts payable ledger, a payroll register and the accounts receivable ledger, each against its own debits and credits, the source totals supplied, the bank statement and the ledger balance, the open period, the posting queue and recurring entries, or the ledger postings and pay schedule it should agree with. The family reads bookkeeping, the record a business keeps of its own transactions in its ledger and journals, and reads the records against each other. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-bookkeeping-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-bookkeeping/.
